reading.body:
Andrew Fields is named on 31 AI lobbying filings, and the clients behind them are almost entirely telecommunications carriers and their trade association.

The client list is the pattern. CTIA, Lumen, Verizon, AT&T, and IAC account for 30 of the 31 filings, with Match Group on one. That is a single industry cluster, not a broad portfolio. The bills named run across both chambers, with 14 Senate bills and 2 House bills listed, all dated 2025 or later.

For AI specifically, this matters because telecom carriers are the physical layer that AI compute depends on. Fiber, data transport, and the networks connecting data centers to users are all regulated at the federal level, and the firms named here have direct commercial interest in how AI-related legislation touches network infrastructure and the buildings that house compute.

What the data does not show is what any of these filings actually say. It records that a bill was named on a filing, not what position was taken, what was spent, or whether the lobbying succeeded. It also does not establish that AI was the subject of every bill listed, only that the filings were categorized as AI-related. The record covers one lobbyist and one firm, and a different lobbyist shares the same name on a separate page.

summary: Andrew Fields is named as a lobbyist on 31 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 40414. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
